snakeplot: Serpentine Plots for Long Timeline, Sequential and Survey Data

Source: R/snakeplot-package.R
snakeplot-package.Rd

snakeplot draws serpentine ("snake") plots: displays in which a long ordered axis (days, time points, positions in a sequence or items of a questionnaire) is folded into parallel bands joined by U-turns. The whole axis fits in one panel, its order is kept, and neighbouring bands can be compared directly. All plots are drawn with base R graphics.

The package covers three kinds of data: event times and continuous measurements within days, categorical state sequences, and responses to rating items, including experience-sampling data collected several times a day. Each plot function draws on the current graphics device; the value it returns invisibly is described on its help page.

Details

Every plot shares the same layout. Bands are stacked from top to bottom; with flow = "snake" they alternate direction so that the axis runs on through each U-turn, and with flow = "natural" every band reads in the same direction, like lines of text. start_from chooses the side of the first band. Most functions default to "snake"; sequence_snake() and timeline_snake() default to "natural".

A serpentine changes the reading of distances. Positions at the ends of adjacent bands are close on the page but far apart on the axis. In activity_snake() and line_snake(), points above one another in adjacent bands share a time of day only when the bands read in the same direction (flow = "natural"). Band labels and U-turn labels give the position on the axis.

Time within days

activity_snake() shows event times, one band per day, as ticks or blocks of their duration. line_snake() draws a continuous series as a line through the days. facet_snake() draws one panel per group.

Sequences

sequence_snake() shows one long categorical sequence as colored blocks along the path. timeline_snake() builds a monthly sequence from phases with start and end dates, such as the positions in a career. multi_snake() shows many sequences as a sequence index or state distribution display (Gabadinho et al., 2011).

Survey and experience-sampling data

survey_snake() shows every response to each item as a tick, with the item mean, optional correlations between adjacent items, and a mode for experience-sampling data with one band per day. survey_sequence() and sequential_dist() show one 100% stacked bar per item, with diverging or single-hue colors (see Heiberger & Robbins, 2014, on stacked bars for rating scales). snake_palette() and snake_palettes provide colors for response levels.

Data

ema_emotions, student_survey and ema_beeps come from a 14-day experience-sampling study of university students (Neubauer & Schmiedek, 2024).

References

Gabadinho, A., Ritschard, G., Müller, N. S., & Studer, M. (2011). Analyzing and visualizing state sequences in R with TraMineR. Journal of Statistical Software, 40(4), 1-37. doi:10.18637/jss.v040.i04

Heiberger, R. M., & Robbins, N. B. (2014). Design of diverging stacked bar charts for Likert scales and other applications. Journal of Statistical Software, 57(5), 1-32. doi:10.18637/jss.v057.i05

Neubauer, A. B., & Schmiedek, F. (2024). Approaching academic adjustment on multiple time scales. Zeitschrift fuer Erziehungswissenschaft, 27(1), 147-168. doi:10.1007/s11618-023-01182-8
